stories.title: Z.ai moves 750B-parameter GLM-5.4 to a loop transformer architecture
stories.summary: Z.ai is giving its flagship GLM-5.4 model a loop architecture that reruns 28 layers twice, which it says lets the 750B-parameter model match 2-3 trillion parameter rivals.
stories.more: The loop design re-executes a block of 28 layers a second time, a technique Z.ai says allows the 750-billion-parameter GLM-5.4 to match the performance of models with 2 to 3 trillion parameters. So far, benchmark scores have only been published for a smaller 30-billion-parameter test model, not the full flagship. Z.ai is positioning GLM-5.4 as the start of what it calls "Generalized Coding," where code generation extends to producing videos, games, and CAD models. The move follows OpenAI into loop transformer territory, according to The Decoder.

stories.title: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra solves math theorem no other AI could crack
stories.summary: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra produced a machine-verifiable Lean proof of Smoktunowicz's gap theorem, inventing its own approach after finding gaps in existing math libraries.
stories.more: GPT-6.2 Astra independently generated a machine-verifiable Lean proof of Smoktunowicz's gap theorem, which Vals AI says is the first of its kind. The model devised its own proof strategy because key foundational results were missing from Mathlib, the Lean math library. On the Autoform-Hard benchmark, Astra now leads the leaderboard, solving 49 of 56 tasks. No other AI system has previously cracked this particular theorem, according to the report.

stories.title: US spies tracked Nvidia scandal figure's China intelligence ties for a year
stories.summary: US intelligence agencies reportedly monitored contacts between Alice Huang and China's Ministry of State Security for over a year, parallel to her affair with then-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
stories.more: The surveillance, reported by the New York Times, tracked contacts between Alice Huang and China's Ministry of State Security for more than a year. It ran in parallel with her secret affair with then-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Federal investigators are now examining whether a network of Southeast Asian companies was used to smuggle AI chips into China in violation of export controls. Jensen Huang is scheduled to testify before the US House of Representatives on December 1.

stories.title: Meta's Alexandr Wang says AI industry isn't ready for what's next
stories.summary: Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang says a recent AI-assisted proof sketch of the Riemann Hypothesis shows superintelligence is approaching faster than the industry is prepared for.
stories.more: Wang's comments followed a recent AI-assisted proof sketch of the Riemann Hypothesis, a longstanding unsolved problem in mathematics. He described the breakthrough as a clear signal that artificial superintelligence could arrive sooner than many expect. As Meta's Chief AI Officer, Wang's remarks carry weight inside one of the largest AI labs. The underlying proof sketch itself, and how it was produced, were not detailed in the available excerpt.

stories.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after board review
stories.summary: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO and board chair, about two weeks after he resigned amid affair allegations, with support from US officials including President Trump.
stories.more: The board said it was satisfied with Huang's candor and his ability to lead Nvidia after a series of discussions and meetings with him. Huang had resigned roughly two weeks earlier, following allegations of multiple affairs, including with a direct report, and claims that he had mistreated employees. President Trump publicly endorsed the board's decision, saying the US government has no evidence of wrongdoing, while urging Nvidia to continue its own export-control investigation. Coverage framed the reversal as swift, noting Nvidia lasted only about two weeks without Huang at the helm, and described a broadly celebratory reaction from other tech leaders.

stories.title: Sierra doubles valuation to $30B on AI customer service demand
stories.summary: Enterprise AI customer-experience startup Sierra, co-founded by Bret Taylor, raised a $1.75 billion Series F that doubled its valuation to $30 billion in six months.
stories.more: The round values Sierra at $30 billion, double its valuation of six months prior, reflecting fast-growing demand for AI in customer experience (CX). Sierra was co-founded by Bret Taylor, the former co-CEO of Salesforce. The company announced the $1.75 billion Series F on Monday. Further details on investors or planned use of the funds were not included in the available coverage.
